newsitem.title: QATAR: Qatar, Philippines sign economic cooperation pact.
newsitem.headline: Qatar, Philippines sign economic cooperation pact.

text.p: Qatar on Monday signed an economic, commercial and technical cooperation agreement with the Philippines and agreed in principle to supply gas to the Asian country.
Visiting Philippines President Fidel Ramos signed the memorandum of understanding to set up a joint commission to boost ties with the oil and gas-rich Gulf Arab state.

Qatar's Minister of Energy and Industry Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah said he met with Philippines officials accompanying Ramos and they discussed the possibility of exporting liquefied natural gas (LNG) and liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) to Manila.
"In principle, we have agreed to supply our gas to the Philippines, but the volume and other details have to be worked out," he told reporters.
Sales of Qatari gas to the Philippines would add to Doha's growing customer base of power utilities in Asia, where it already has firm sales agreements in Japan and South Korea.
Ramos, who traveled to Bahrain later in the day, is urging Gulf Arab states to pump capital into his country's oil industry and economy.
Addressing Qatari businessmen, Ramos said investment opportunities in his country included eco-tourism, processing industries and consumer-related and downstream ventures.

"The deregulation and liberalisation of our key industries, such as telecommunications, banking, insurance, shipping, aviation, wholesale trade ... and the privatisation of government- controlled corporations or their components has opened vast opportunities for Middle East investors," he said.

Qatar is home to around 33,000 Filipino workers, but trade between the two countries has been less than one percent of the Philippines' overseas trade. Bilateral trade in the 11 months to November 1996 amounted to $41.62 million, with Manila posting a $38.12 million deficit.
